turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Well, I’m here because I keep making these little mistakes that are starting to bother me. Like I’ll write the wrong time down on a senior-center class sheet, or I’ll measure a board and still cut it just a bit short because I skipped over some small print. It’s not huge things, but it keeps happening.

symptom_reasoning.S001: The patient reports recurrent small mistakes, including writing an incorrect time and overlooking small print when measuring a board.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been having any trouble with your eyesight?
turns.patient_response: I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything obvious with my eyesight, but I haven’t really thought about it much.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been having any difficulty reading small print?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure, honestly. I haven’t really noticed small print being a problem, at least not in a way that stood out to me.

turns.doctor_question: When you look at writing on a page, do the words or numbers ever look blurry?
turns.patient_response: I can’t say I’ve really noticed them looking blurry. If they are, it hasn’t been obvious to me.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever miss things that are off to one side when you’re looking at a page or object?
turns.patient_response: No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed missing things off to the side when I’m looking at something.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually worried or nervous lately?
turns.patient_response: Not especially, no. I mean, I get concerned about things now and then like anyone, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually worried or nervous lately.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient states they have not been unusually worried lately, while acknowledging only ordinary occasional concerns.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient explicitly says they have not been unusually nervous lately.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been forgetting recent conversations or appointments?
turns.patient_response: Sometimes, yeah. It’s not always that I forget the whole conversation, but I don’t take in what was said. Like my wife will be looking right at me and say something like, “Dave, the cards are in the hall closet now,” and then a minute later I realize I heard her talking but I don’t know where she said they were.

symptom_reasoning.S003: He reports hearing his wife speak directly to him but not taking in the information she said, with this occurring sometimes.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had any trouble hearing what people say?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think I have trouble hearing, no. It’s more like I hear that someone’s talking, but sometimes I don’t really catch it unless I’m paying attention.

symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient reports sometimes not catching what someone says unless paying attention, despite hearing that they are talking.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find it hard to stay focused on what someone is saying?
turns.patient_response: Yes, sometimes. Like I said, my wife can be looking right at me telling me something simple, like, “Dave, the cards are in the hall closet now,” and a minute later I realize I heard her talking, but I didn’t really take in where she said they were.

symptom_reasoning.S003: Patient reports sometimes hearing his wife speaking directly to him but failing to take in the content of what she said.

turns.doctor_question: If you make a point to pay close attention when someone tells you something, are you usually able to remember it afterward?
turns.patient_response: If I really make myself pay attention, I do better, yes. It’s more when I’m not locked in on it. My wife can tell me something plain, like where she moved the cards, and I hear her voice, but a minute later I don’t know where she said they were.

symptom_reasoning.S003: He reports hearing his wife's voice but, when not deliberately focused, being unable a minute later to recall the information she told him.

turns.doctor_question: When was your last eye exam?
turns.patient_response: I’m not sure, honestly. It’s been a while, but I don’t remember exactly when.

turns.doctor_question: Do you ever look right at words or numbers and still have trouble recognizing what they are?
turns.patient_response: I don’t think so. I mean, I might have to look twice if I’m distracted or the print is small, but I haven’t really noticed looking straight at a word or number and not recognizing it.

turns.doctor_question: Have these problems started to interfere with things like managing your bills or medications?
turns.patient_response: Not so much bills or medications, no. It’s been more with plans and things I’m supposed to help with. I’ve had enough mix-ups that I stepped back from helping lead a couple DIY workshops, and my wife usually double-checks plans now so I don’t mess up family visits or things at the center.

turns.doctor_question: Do you now need help managing your finances?
turns.patient_response: No, I don’t think I need help with finances right now. I can still manage that okay.

turns.doctor_question: Do you need help keeping track of your appointments?
turns.patient_response: Not usually just the appointment by itself. It’s more when I’ve got a few errands, maybe a workshop to get ready for, and an appointment all on the same day. I have trouble putting it all in order, and I’ll start one thing, stop, then end up rushing around at the end.

symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient reports difficulty ordering and managing multiple same-day errands, workshop preparation, and an appointment, leading to fragmented task completion and last-minute rushing.

turns.doctor_question: Because of these thinking problems, do you now need someone else to take over any of your usual day-to-day tasks?
turns.patient_response: Not take over, no. I still do my regular day-to-day things. But the mix-ups have made me step back from helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops, and my wife double-checks plans now so I don’t throw off family visits or things at the center.

turns.doctor_question: Because of these thinking problems, do you need help shopping on your own?
turns.patient_response: No, I don’t need help shopping on my own. I can handle that. Maybe I take a list with me sometimes, but I’m not needing someone to go with me or do it for me.

turns.doctor_question: Do these thinking problems ever make you unable to complete a task that you used to handle on your own?
turns.patient_response: Not unable exactly, but I’ve had to back off from some things I used to do. Like helping lead a couple of the DIY workshops — the mix-ups were causing problems. And my wife double-checks plans now, so I don’t mess up family visits or things going on at the center.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel these thinking problems are a clear change from how you used to function before?
turns.patient_response: Not really a clear change, no. I mean, I’ve had this kind of thing since I was a kid. Even in elementary school, teachers would say I was bright, but I’d forget my books, lose homework, or just stare out the window unless someone kept me on track.

symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient reports forgetting books and losing homework since elementary school.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being prone to staring out the window and needing external redirection to stay on task, consistent with distractibility.

turns.patient_response: Yes, school for sure.
